reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-provided param value, which reaches the HTML response after being encoded by ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(), but the encoding is applied to the file path string, not the user input directly, making the XSS vulnerability exploitable. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value is param, which directly controls the file path construction in new java.io.File(..., bar), allowing path traversal attacks. Case TP: at least one alert-TP.

evidence.note: User input retrieved via getParameterMap and assigned to param
User input flows through doSomething() to bar, which is used in file path construction
fileTarget constructed using bar (user-controlled) as part of path
